Chapter One — The Beginning of the Road: Drawn into the World of Shadows
Imagine living in a place where fear isn’t just something you feel every now and then — it’s woven into daily life. Even if you’ve got nothing to hide, being safe becomes this constant obsession. That’s exactly how things were for a young man growing up in an ordinary Syrian city. He’d hear neighbors whispering about these mysterious “men of shadow” — the ones who always seemed to know everything.
Now, joining the security forces wasn’t ever his childhood dream. It was more like a path that showed up when life left him with few options. In a world where personal safety and opportunity seemed out of reach, those doors only opened if you went through the security apparatus.
Back then, joining the intelligence services felt less like getting a job and more like scoring a ticket to a whole different reality. It wasn’t just about power or influence — it was about this strange sense of safety, a feeling that maybe, just maybe, you could finally breathe easy. Most people who stepped into that world weren’t out to serve some ideology. For a lot of them, it was about keeping their families safe, protecting themselves, or sometimes just pure curiosity — wanting to know what really goes on behind closed doors.
At first, things seemed straightforward: a formal interview, questions about your family background, a test of your loyalty. But it didn’t take long to realize — this wasn’t just another job. It was a complete shift in how you lived. Old friendships started to change, and even simple conversations began to feel loaded with hidden meanings.
Picture this: one afternoon, our young man is sitting in a café with his childhood friend. Suddenly, joking about politics or sharing a harmless story feels risky. He can’t quite be himself anymore. Every word could be twisted later on — seen in a completely different light.
Joining this world isn’t just about watching others. It’s about watching yourself, all the time. Every move, every glance — you feel like someone, somewhere, is always keeping tabs on you. Even your coworkers aren’t safe to trust, because who knows? Maybe someone’s been told to watch you, too. The smallest thing, like being late to work, could be seen as a sign that you’re not loyal enough, or that you might be hiding something. One day, a new recruit gets a simple comment from his boss about being late. But underneath, the message is clear: “We’re watching you. Don’t forget it.”
Over time, fear starts to become part of your daily routine. And it’s not just fear of strangers — you start feeling wary of your own friends, your coworkers, even yourself. One night, a young man comes home late and finds his mother waiting up for him, anxious. She doesn’t ask him about his day. She just gives him a look that’s equal parts pride and fear. In that moment, he realizes his life isn’t just his own anymore. He’s now part of something much bigger, something that forces him to be careful with every tiny detail.
That’s how the journey into the world of Syrian intelligence really begins. Sometimes it’s about need, sometimes ambition, and sometimes just fear. But once you step inside this closed circle, everything becomes a test. Every relationship, every moment, is up for questioning. And with each passing day, it becomes clearer — getting out of this world is a whole lot harder than getting in.
